why: R2 duplication. Cards 54 and 55 already test both halves of this card's claim (stroke volume = the per-beat volume, cardiac output = the per-minute volume), and they carry the actual numbers besides, so this card re-tested the same two definitions from TABLE 6-7 (card-rules #12). revised_Text: Cardiac output is the product of two values: {{c1::heart rate}} and {{c1::stroke volume}}.
revised_Back_Extra:
Mechanism: written out, CO = HR × SV, so 70 beats/min × 75 mL/beat gives 5,250 mL/min, or 5.25 L/min.

Distinguish: stroke volume is the per-beat volume moved by the left ventricle, while cardiac output is the per-minute volume.

why: R2 duplication. The c1 blank re-tested 'name systemic vascular resistance from its definition', which card 62 already tests off the p588 body text; card 62's own Distinguish line even states this card's exact definition, so the two cards were one fact carded twice (card-rules #12). Kept the term visible as the anchor and re-aimed the card at what only TABLE 6-7 adds: the pulmonary exclusion and the resistance-to-pressure relationship. Verified verbatim against p588 ('all blood vessels except the pulmonary vessels') and TABLE 6-7 ('the higher the SVR, the smaller the container; therefore, the higher the pressure of blood within the vessel').
revised_Text: Systemic vascular resistance covers the resistance to blood flow in every blood vessel except {{c1::the pulmonary vessels}}, and as it rises the container the blood must fill gets {{c2::smaller::larger or smaller}}.
revised_Back_Extra:
Mechanism: the same volume of blood packed into a smaller container sits at a higher pressure, which is why a rising systemic vascular resistance drives the pressure inside the vessels up.

Cue: the word systemic is what excludes the lung circulation from this value.

revised_Text: The {{c1::cerebrum::brain subdivision}} is the largest part of the brain, about {{c2::three-fourths}} of it, and it runs the brain's higher functions: {{c3::sensory interpretation}}, {{c3::speech}}, {{c3::reasoning and learning}}, {{c3::fine motor control}}, and {{c3::managing emotions}}.
